## Budget Feasibility Check

### Path A — Compact Drill (budget-friendly)
| Category | Cost |
|---|---|
| Personnel (geo + driller) | 900 cr |
| Compact drill | 12,000 cr |
| Bits ×3 | 2,400 cr |
| Hammer ×1 | 1,500 cr |
| Geological survey | 500 cr |
| Deliveries (2 orders) | 400 cr |
| Operating costs | 600 cr |
| **Total** | **~18,300 cr** |
| **Remaining from 39k** | **~20,700 cr** |

### Path B — Advanced Drill (premium)
| Category | Cost |
|---|---|
| Personnel (geo + driller + helper) | 1,150 cr |
| Advanced drill | 22,000 cr |
| Bits ×3 | 3,600 cr |
| Hammer ×1 | 1,500 cr |
| Geological survey | 500 cr |
| Deliveries (2 orders) | 400 cr |
| Operating costs | 600 cr |
| **Total** | **~29,750 cr** |
| **Remaining from 39k** | **~9,250 cr** |

### M3 Completion Reward (proposed)
- Contract payment: **25,000 cr** (sufficient to sustain into future missions)
- Bonus for under-budget: +5,000 cr
- Bonus for speed: +3,000 cr

---

## Conclusion

**Both paths are financially viable.** A player who spent heavily in M2 (down to ~35k) can still afford the compact drill path with ~16,700 cr margin. The advanced drill path is tight but achievable, rewarding careful M2 spending.

The M3 reward (25k base) ensures the player has ~45-55k entering M4, matching the escalation curve.

### Safety Rails
- If cash < 15,000 at M3 start → mentor suggests compact drill
- If cash < 12,000 → contract includes equipment stipend (5,000 cr advance)
- Player can never be permanently stuck — worst case they take the free survey + compact path
